title: Bearing True Witness
sub: Faith and Truth in a World of Deception · Grades 5–8 · Religion · 30 minutes
objective: Students will understand how the Eighth Commandment applies to modern challenges including deepfakes and misinformation, recognize that bearing true witness requires both careful verification *and* moral courage, and create a personal commitment to truth-telling.
materials: Catechism of the Catholic Church (paragraphs 2464–2513, selections)
connection: **Option 1 — Visit:** Spirit photography in the exhibition shows how visual deception exploited grief. William Mumler exploited people’s vulnerability for profit — bearing false witness through images rather than words.

steps.title: Opening prayer
script: Jesus said to him, ‘I am the way, and the truth, and the life.’ (John 14:6)
*“Lord, help us to be seekers and speakers of truth. Give us the wisdom to recognize falsehood, the courage to speak honestly, and the charity to do so with love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.”*

screen.prayer: Lord, help us to be seekers and speakers of truth. Give us the wisdom to recognize falsehood, the courage to speak honestly, and the charity to do so with love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

steps.purpose: Begin by asking for the wisdom and courage the lesson is about.

steps.title: The Spirit Photography Deception
script: Display spirit photography examples from the 1860s–1900s.

*“After the Civil War, a photographer named William Mumler claimed he could photograph spirits of the dead. He charged grieving families large sums for these fake images — double exposures. He bore false witness through images. Today we’ll explore what the Eighth Commandment teaches about truth in a world of deepfakes and viral misinformation.”*

screen.question: He bore false witness through images.

steps.purpose: A fake from history sets up the commandment and its meaning today.

steps.title: The Eighth Commandment
script: **Unpack:** Originally about courtroom testimony, but the Church teaches it extends to all truth-telling. Read CCC 2464: “The eighth commandment forbids misrepresenting the truth in our relations with others.”

verse.text: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

steps.purpose: Read the commandment, and how the Church extends it to all truth-telling.

steps.title: The truth will set you free
script: You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. (John 8:32)

verse.text: You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

steps.purpose: Truth as freedom, not only as a rule.

steps.title: Bearing false witness
script: **Discussion:** What are ways we can “bear false witness” without being in a courtroom? (Gossip, rumors, sharing unverified info, manipulating images.) Did the spirit photographer bear false witness even though he used images, not words? (Yes.)

screen.question: What are ways we can “bear false witness” without being in a courtroom? Did the spirit photographer bear false witness even though he used images, not words?

steps.purpose: Widen the commandment from the courtroom to everyday words and images.

steps.title: Deepfakes and Our Responsibility
script: *“Spirit photography was the deepfake of the 1860s. Today, AI can create videos of people saying things they never said.”*
**Discuss:** Why is this a moral issue and not just a technology issue? What responsibilities do we have as Christians when we encounter information online?

screen.question: Why is this a moral issue and not just a technology issue? What responsibilities do we have as Christians when we encounter information online?

steps.purpose: From the 1860s to AI: the same moral question.
students: Today, AI can create videos of people saying things they never said.

steps.title: Two dimensions of bearing true witness
script: Two dimensions of bearing true witness today:
**1. Verification:** Seek truth before we speak or share. Check sources, be skeptical of sensational claims.
**2. Moral courage:** Speaking up when difficult — correcting misinformation, admitting when wrong, refusing gossip.

screen.caption: Two dimensions of bearing true witness today

cells: Seek truth before we speak or share. Check sources, be skeptical of sensational claims.
Speaking up when difficult — correcting misinformation, admitting when wrong, refusing gossip.

steps.purpose: Two things bearing true witness needs: careful checking and the courage to speak.

steps.title: Our Commitment to Truth
script: As a class, create a “Commitment to Truth” pledge on chart paper. Guide students toward including:
I will verify before I share
I will not spread gossip or rumors
I will have courage to speak truth, even when difficult
I will admit when I am wrong or uncertain
I will treat others’ reputations as sacred
steps.purpose: The class writes its own pledge together on chart paper.
students: I will verify before I share
I will not spread gossip or rumors
I will have courage to speak truth, even when difficult
I will admit when I am wrong or uncertain
I will treat others’ reputations as sacred

steps.title: Closing prayer
script: *“Lord, you are the Way, the Truth, and the Life. Help us to be witnesses to your truth in our words, our actions, and what we share with others. Give us wisdom to recognize deception and courage to speak honestly. Through Christ our Lord, Amen.”*

screen.prayer: Lord, you are the Way, the Truth, and the Life. Help us to be witnesses to your truth in our words, our actions, and what we share with others. Give us wisdom to recognize deception and courage to speak honestly. Through Christ our Lord, Amen.

steps.purpose: Close by giving the pledge back to God in prayer.
